Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

ugly adjective

also ugliness, unattractive, homely, plain, homely (plain), plain (not pretty), unsightly

classical

Cic. Inv. 1.35 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 158, 399

dēfōrmis, dēfōrme

misshapen, ugly

Lewis & Short: departing from the right shape, unsightly, ugly; of things and people, and morally, disgraceful.

Other words

  • turpis, turpe — ugly; shameful

    also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.126 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 158, 399

  • invenustus, invenusta, invenustum — unattractive, without charm

    also used · classical · Cat. 10.4 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 158, 400

  • īnspeciōsus, īnspeciōsa, īnspeciōsum — plain, unshapely

    also used · classical · Traupman 153; Petr. Fragm. 74.8 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 329

    Lewis & Short cites only a fragment of Petronius.

  • dēfōrmitās, dēfōrmitātis f. — ugliness, deformity

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Liv. 2.23 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 158, 399

    Traupman also gives it for “lack of good taste”; Lewis & Short has it of an uncouth style (Quint. 6.1.37).

Examples

  • dēfōrmitās

    lack of good tasteTraupman 390

See also attractive.
